api-optional-default.rationale: The route supplies a documented response or request default only for an absent optional value; storage and authorization failures retain non-success behavior.
api-optional-default.test: affected HTTP route specs and error_squelch_architecture_spec
api-optional-default.removal_condition: Remove when the field becomes required or its default moves into a versioned schema decoder.

authority-state-failure.rationale: The implementation discards only an implementation-specific source value while preserving a typed authority failure, read-only latch, or rejected operation.
authority-state-failure.removal_condition: Remove when the source evidence is needed for recovery policy or operator diagnostics.

authorization-concealment.rationale: Authorization failures are deliberately collapsed to a non-authorizing response so storage details cannot leak; the request remains denied.
authorization-concealment.removal_condition: Remove only if a new public auth error taxonomy preserves the same concealment guarantee.

boundary-validation-failure.rationale: Boundary parsing maps implementation-specific parse or conversion errors to a stable caller-facing invalid-input failure; success is never returned.
boundary-validation-failure.test: affected command, route, plugin specs and error_squelch_architecture_spec
boundary-validation-failure.removal_condition: Remove when the public error contract begins carrying structured source diagnostics.

bounded-authority-default.rationale: The fallback is conservative, bounded, and fail-closed for unavailable optional authority metadata; it cannot widen writes, reclaim data early, or bypass a durability latch.
bounded-authority-default.owner: storage, durability, GC, and v4 control owners
bounded-authority-default.test: durability, storage, GC, v4 control, and error_squelch_architecture specs
bounded-authority-default.removal_condition: Remove when the value becomes mandatory authority or can be propagated through a fallible caller.

candidate-format-probe.rationale: Recovery or parser code rejects one non-authoritative candidate and continues bounded discovery; authoritative readers still return corruption when no valid candidate exists.
candidate-format-probe.test: corruption_hardening_spec, repair specs, parser specs, and error_squelch_architecture_spec
candidate-format-probe.removal_condition: Remove if the skipped candidate becomes part of acknowledged complete traversal rather than bounded recovery discovery.

checked-arithmetic-composition.rationale: Result-to-option conversion composes a checked numeric conversion with further checked arithmetic and ends in a typed overflow or resource error; no zero or truncated value is accepted.
checked-arithmetic-composition.removal_condition: Remove when a shared checked-accounting helper can express the chain without an intermediate Option.

contractual-configuration-default.rationale: The absence case uses a documented default or lower-precedence configuration source; malformed present values are rejected by the central resolver.
contractual-configuration-default.test: config_shadow_spec, run configuration specs, CLI specs, and error_squelch_architecture_spec
contractual-configuration-default.removal_condition: Remove when the property becomes mandatory or its default is deleted from the frozen registry.

derived-cache-or-search-miss.rationale: The broad branch represents an ordered lookup miss or cache non-admission; callers retain the exact storage result or retry through authoritative state.
derived-cache-or-search-miss.removal_condition: Remove if this branch can observe an I/O or corruption error rather than a local miss.

derived-exact-fallback.rationale: A failed optional derived lookup becomes absence only before an exact authoritative fallback, scan, or non-admission path.
derived-exact-fallback.owner: query, index, cache, and search runtime
derived-exact-fallback.test: query/index equivalence, cache pressure, and error_squelch_architecture specs
derived-exact-fallback.removal_condition: Remove if callers stop performing the exact fallback or the derived artifact becomes correctness-bearing.

derived-state-default.rationale: Absent derived index, cache, or plan metadata selects the exact scan/rebuild path or disables retention; it never fabricates authoritative membership.
derived-state-default.test: query, index, cache pressure, and error_squelch_architecture specs
derived-state-default.removal_condition: Remove when derived state becomes mandatory and durably versioned.

derived-status-control.rationale: Success status controls cache retention, event delivery, or derived publication only; authority remains readable and failures choose eviction, retry, or exact fallback.
derived-status-control.test: cache, index, event, namespace mutation, and error_squelch_architecture specs
derived-status-control.removal_condition: Remove if the status begins controlling an acknowledged authoritative transition.

diagnostic-partial-output.rationale: A CLI diagnostic continues only to report additional independent evidence or complete controlled shutdown; the failed sub-result remains visible and is not a database success.
diagnostic-partial-output.test: CLI command specs, soak worker specs, and error_squelch_architecture_spec
diagnostic-partial-output.removal_condition: Remove when the diagnostic output schema can carry all partial failures as one structured result.

fail-closed-status-control.rationale: The status probe grants no capability and acknowledges no write on error; unavailable authority is treated as absent, denied, or read-only.
fail-closed-status-control.test: auth, durability poison, namespace mutation, and error_squelch_architecture specs
fail-closed-status-control.removal_condition: Remove when the caller can propagate a typed authority error without weakening concealment.

fatal-build-boundary.rationale: The build script terminates compilation when required checked-in or generated assets cannot be produced; continuing would create a knowingly incomplete binary.
fatal-build-boundary.removal_condition: Remove an entry when the build step becomes fallible to Cargo without producing an incomplete artifact.

format-or-header-probe.rationale: The conversion probes an optional representation, header, timestamp, or parser alternative; failure selects another bounded representation or a typed unsupported result.
format-or-header-probe.test: parser, range, route header, locator, and error_squelch_architecture specs
format-or-header-probe.removal_condition: Remove when the input contract accepts only one representation and can return its parse error directly.

http-terminal-error.rationale: The route intentionally conceals internal error detail while returning a non-success HTTP status or a security-preserving generic response; no mutation is acknowledged as successful.
http-terminal-error.test: affected HTTP route specs and error_squelch_architecture_spec
http-terminal-error.removal_condition: Remove when the route adopts a structured safe error envelope that retains the classified cause.

http-terminal-or-postcommit-evidence.rationale: The HTTP path either returns a terminal non-success response or preserves an already durable primary result while recording failure of optional notification, cleanup, or derived publication.
http-terminal-or-postcommit-evidence.owner: HTTP route and post-commit side-effect owners
http-terminal-or-postcommit-evidence.test: affected route specs, soft-failure metrics specs, and error_squelch_architecture_spec
http-terminal-or-postcommit-evidence.removal_condition: Split or remove the entry when the side effect becomes part of the acknowledged mutation contract.

iterator-terminal-state.rationale: The iterator records that a previously returned decode error has fused traversal; the error itself is yielded once and no empty-complete result is fabricated.
iterator-terminal-state.test: v4 iterator and malformed fixture specs plus error_squelch_architecture_spec
iterator-terminal-state.removal_condition: Remove when the iterator state uses an explicit terminal enum rather than probing the prior Result.

legacy-infallible-boundary.rationale: A historical infallible public constructor delegates to the checked constructor and terminates locally; all production startup paths use the fallible API.
legacy-infallible-boundary.removal_condition: Remove when the next breaking API revision deletes the infallible compatibility constructor.

local-status-control.rationale: The status is consumed immediately for local command, channel, or control flow and does not discard acknowledged storage failure.
local-status-control.removal_condition: Replace with an exhaustive match if the error variant becomes semantically distinct.

optional-cleanup-evidence.rationale: Failure affects optional cleanup or secondary evidence after the primary result; it is logged, metered, or returned as a warning without falsifying the primary outcome.
optional-cleanup-evidence.test: backup, lifecycle, lost-found, scanner, and error_squelch_architecture specs
optional-cleanup-evidence.removal_condition: Remove when cleanup is promoted into the primary operation's atomic contract.

optional-data-default.rationale: An absent optional document, metadata, parser, or presentation value receives the documented neutral representation; malformed authoritative containers still fail.
optional-data-default.test: parser, range, query, content-type, and error_squelch_architecture specs
optional-data-default.removal_condition: Remove when the value becomes required by its public or persistent schema.

optional-observability-default.rationale: Unavailable secondary telemetry is represented as unknown, degraded, or a conservative bounded value and never changes storage or authorization correctness.
optional-observability-default.removal_condition: Remove when the platform exposes a mandatory fallible metric that callers can represent directly.

ordered-optional-precedence.rationale: The expression chooses the next documented optional source or compatibility spelling after absence; it does not recover from an authoritative persistence failure.
ordered-optional-precedence.test: config_shadow_spec, index config specs, and error_squelch_architecture_spec
ordered-optional-precedence.removal_condition: Remove when the older source or spelling leaves the supported compatibility contract.

parser-alternative-probe.rationale: The parser or serializer tries a bounded alternative and either returns a valid result, another valid error envelope, or an explicit unsupported value; it never claims complete parsed data after required decoding fails.
parser-alternative-probe.test: native parser, indexing pipeline, plugin runtime, locator, and error_squelch_architecture specs
parser-alternative-probe.removal_condition: Remove when the format has one mandatory representation or the fallback ABI is retired.

plugin-compatibility-default.rationale: The plugin adapter supplies a bounded ABI compatibility default for an omitted optional field; malformed required host state is rejected.
plugin-compatibility-default.removal_condition: Remove when the older plugin ABI is no longer supported.

plugin-error-envelope.rationale: Plugin boundary serialization falls back only to another valid bounded error envelope; malformed host data never becomes a successful plugin response.
plugin-error-envelope.removal_condition: Remove when the plugin ABI provides an infallible fixed error frame.

postcommit-derived-reconciliation.rationale: The primary namespace or durability transition is already hard-acknowledged; derived cache, event, index, or reconciliation failure is metered and repaired from authority.
postcommit-derived-reconciliation.test: namespace_mutation specs, indexing specs, SSE specs, and error_squelch_architecture_spec
postcommit-derived-reconciliation.removal_condition: Remove when the derived effect joins the hard acknowledgement boundary or receives a durable retry task.

presence-feature-toggle.rationale: Only environment-variable presence controls an explicit debug, timing, rate-limit, or dangerous-operation opt-in; the variable's contents are intentionally irrelevant.
presence-feature-toggle.test: GC, snapshot, startup safety, magic-link, and error_squelch_architecture specs
presence-feature-toggle.removal_condition: Remove when the toggle moves into typed central configuration.

redundant-authority-selection.rationale: One redundant header or control copy failed validation; selection succeeds only from another independently valid copy and rejects the state when neither copy is valid.
redundant-authority-selection.test: v4 database header, control fixture, file_header, and error_squelch_architecture specs
redundant-authority-selection.removal_condition: Remove if redundancy is retired or validation no longer independently proves the selected copy.

retryable-background-operation.rationale: The background operation records visible failure evidence and retries on the bounded worker cadence or next startup instead of acknowledging completion.
retryable-background-operation.owner: task, cron, cleanup, integrity, and webhook workers
retryable-background-operation.test: task worker, cron, index cleanup, integrity scanner, webhook, and error_squelch_architecture specs
retryable-background-operation.removal_condition: Remove when the worker gains a durable per-attempt terminal record that can propagate the exact error.

typed-format-failure.rationale: The original error detail is normalized into the frozen malformed-input taxonomy while the operation remains an error and no partial value is returned.
typed-format-failure.test: v4 format fixture specs, corruption_hardening_spec, and error_squelch_architecture_spec
typed-format-failure.removal_condition: Remove when retaining the source error is part of the frozen diagnostic contract.

unwind-cleanup-evidence.rationale: Drop is only an unwind or last-resort cleanup path; normal completion is explicit, while failure here is logged or latched and cannot turn a failed primary operation into success.
unwind-cleanup-evidence.test: poison, shutdown, GC, KV page, and error_squelch_architecture specs
unwind-cleanup-evidence.removal_condition: Remove when the resource can require explicit completion at every construction site and no unwind guard remains necessary.

validated-local-invariant.rationale: The conversion or branch follows an exact bounds, registry, constant, or semantic validation in the same local control flow and cannot reinterpret external failure as success.
validated-local-invariant.test: records_spec, v4 format fixture specs, and error_squelch_architecture_spec
validated-local-invariant.removal_condition: Replace the entry with a typed error if its precondition stops being locally exhaustive or accepts external mutable state.
